subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 58-year-old man with alcohol use disorder is brought to the hospital with confusion, unsteady gait, and horizontal nystagmus with ophthalmoplegia. His diet has been poor for several months.
question: Which of the following enzymes of the pentose phosphate pathway requires thiamine pyrophosphate as a cofactor?
explanation_correct: Transketolase, an enzyme of the nonoxidative phase of the pentose phosphate pathway, requires thiamine pyrophosphate (vitamin B1). Thiamine deficiency also impairs pyruvate dehydrogenase and alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase and classically produces Wernicke encephalopathy with confusion, ataxia, and ophthalmoplegia.

explanation_incorrect.B: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase is the rate-limiting enzyme of the oxidative phase and uses NADP+ as an electron acceptor, not thiamine pyrophosphate.
explanation_incorrect.C: 6-Phosphogluconate dehydrogenase is the second dehydrogenase of the oxidative phase and also uses NADP+, not a thiamine cofactor.
explanation_incorrect.D: Phosphopentose isomerase converts ribulose-5-phosphate to ribose-5-phosphate without a thiamine pyrophosphate cofactor.
explanation_incorrect.E: Ribulose-5-phosphate epimerase converts ribulose-5-phosphate to xylulose-5-phosphate and does not require thiamine pyrophosphate.

educationalObjective: Transketolase, a thiamine pyrophosphate-dependent enzyme of the nonoxidative pentose phosphate pathway, is one of the enzymes impaired in thiamine deficiency.
